title: M11: clicking a row (go to its terminal) fails for a tmux session with no feedback in the panel, and puts a 'claude --resume' command on the clipboard
repro: Open Home with a tmux-hosted session listed (atlas).
expected: Its tmux pane comes forward. Failing that, the panel states the failure in the row and offers something that works. The clipboard never gets a command that would start a second claude on a live session.
actual: jump returned {ok:false, cmd:'cd …/atlas && claude --resume <id>'} in 171 ms, and the clipboard write was intercepted. The only feedback was the bubble 'atlas: couldn't find its terminal — resume command copied', drawn behind the panel. The row shows nothing.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S1/timings.json F3 row click (249 ms, ok:false)
truth: atlas alive in tmux pane vp-atlas, registry idle.

why: Clicking atlas's row body (alive in tmux pane vp-atlas, registry busy) returned {ok:false, cmd:'cd .../fleet/atlas && claude --resume <sid>'} in 91 ms and wrote that command to the (intercepted) clipboard; pasting it would start a second claude on a live session. The row showed nothing (noteFor() is defined but never called), and the only feedback, the bubble, drew under the composer. The tmux server's ppid is 1, so hostApp never finds a terminal app for any tmux session.
cause: main.js:714 (resume-command fallback even for a live session); agents.js:326 (hostApp stops at the daemonized tmux server); renderer/app.js:615 (row note never rendered)

title: M11: `/jump <session>` never reaches a tmux session (22/22 failed) and overwrites the clipboard with `claude --resume <id>` for a session that is still live
repro: Home open with a visible fleet row (ember, kestrel, atlas or vibepet; all run in tmux)
Inspect the jump result and the clipboard
expected: The session's tmux pane is brought forward (the registry names the pane), or the panel says exactly why not and offers a working next step; never a clipboard command that would start a second claude on a live session.
actual: 22 of 22 `/jump` runs returned ok:false after 100–281 ms (median 141); every one wrote `cd ~/.vibepet-ultra/fleet/<repo> && claude --resume <session id>` to the clipboard. The user is left to find the pane by hand.
evidence: /Users/christopherharris/projects/vibepet/docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S3/timings.json: "/jump <visible session> (tmux): jump lookup in main → result" (141 ms, n=22)
truth: ember idle (loop) 134–163 s in pane vp-ember:0.0; kestrel idle 132 s, turn ended with a question, pane vp-kestrel:0.0 pid 55946; atlas busy (build.sh); vibepet idle (done)

why: 6/6 `/jump` runs to tmux sessions returned {ok:false}: vibepet x3 in 83-84 ms, plus `/jump` with no name, `/jump a` and `/jump b`. Each one wrote `cd ~/.vibepet-ultra/fleet/vibepet && claude --resume 6101876b-…` to the clipboard (recorded by the stub; unstubbed, it overwrites the user's clipboard). vibepet was live in pane vp-vibepet:0.0 at the time (pid 48221, registry idle). guiHost(pid) = null for all 5 live members: the tmux server is a daemon, so hostApp finds no .app ancestor and jump falls through to the resume command. No tmux path exists, although the registry names the pane.
cause: main.js:700-714 (hostApp null -> clipboard.writeText(resume cmd)); agents.js:326-331 (hostApp only knows .app ancestors)

title: [M10][M12] Approve and Reply cannot reach a tmux-hosted session: send-to answers "couldn't find its tab" and nothing is delivered
repro: Prompt kestrel to end its turn with a yes/no question (row turns 'needs' with Reply)
IPC probe of Approve's call: send-to(kestrel, null)
expected: The reply lands in kestrel's session (new user record, new turn); Approve presses Enter in kestrel's pane.
actual: 3 of 3 replies: note "Couldn't send: couldn't find its tab" 133/211/136 ms after Enter; 0 new transcript records; registry stayed idle. Approve's send-to returned the same {ok:false} for kestrel (89 ms) and beacon (87 ms). The sessions run under a tmux server with no .app ancestor (GUI host = null), which is the only host send-to knows.
truth: end_turn 'Should the deploy script have unit tests?' at 02:00:09.6Z; registry idle; tmux vp-kestrel pane %8

title: [M11] Jump never reaches a tmux session: terminal not raised, tmux client not switched, and it copies `claude --resume <id>` for live sessions
repro: Have a Terminal.app window with a tmux client attached to the fleet (kestrel's session)
Click the title of each row (6 members x3)
expected: ≤1 s: Terminal comes forward with its tmux client on that session's pane.
actual: 18 of 18 jumps returned {ok:false} (click→result median 154 ms); frontmost app unchanged 18/18; the tmux client stayed on kestrel for jumps to beacon/atlas/delta/ember/vibepet; each wrote `cd ~/.vibepet-ultra/fleet/<member> && claude --resume <session-id>` to the clipboard (recorded) — for the live sessions (kestrel, beacon, atlas, delta, vibepet) that would start a second claude on the same session.
truth: kestrel waiting(permission prompt), beacon waiting(input needed), atlas busy (build.sh), delta busy (fan-out), vibepet idle, ember exited; tmux client /dev/ttys012 on vp-kestrel

why: Reply 'yes' ×3 on kestrel's needs row: 'Couldn't send: couldn't find its tab' 164–258 ms after Enter, 0 new transcript lines, registry stayed idle. Approve on kestrel's stuck row ×2: 'Couldn't approve: couldn't find its tab' (117–143 ms), kestrel still waiting(permission prompt), 0 new lines. IPC probe send-to(null) kestrel/beacon: 4/4 the same. Process chain: claude → /bin/bash → /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux (ppid 1) → launchd, so hostApp() finds no .app and send-to refuses; there is no tmux send-keys path (no 'tmux' in main.js, agents.js or app.js).

7/7 row-title jumps on live tmux sessions (vibepet idle ×3, atlas busy ×3, kestrel with its permission dialog up ×1) returned {ok:false} in 96–141 ms (median 123). The frontmost app was unchanged each time, and each wrote 'cd ~/.vibepet-ultra/fleet/<member> && claude --resume <sid>' to the (recorded) clipboard: a second claude on a session that is live in its pane. The jump path has no tmux code at all, and hostApp walks only claude's own ancestors (bash → tmux server → launchd), so an attached tmux client can never be found or switched. Not re-run with a Terminal tmux client attached (that opens a window on the user's screen); the code makes that outcome deterministic.

title: [M11] Jump key lands on no tmux pane and copies `claude --resume <id>` over the clipboard on every press
repro: Have any fleet session (tmux, no attached client) in the jump queue
Press the jump key (OS-level ⌥⌘J, or the registered handler)
Inspect the jump IPC result, clipboard writes (stubbed), and `tmux display -p -t vp-<member>:0.0 '#{session_attached} #{window_active} #{pane_active}'` before/after
expected: The session's tmux window/pane is selected and the terminal hosting it is focused (the registry carries the pane, e.g. vp-kestrel:@W.%P), or the pet says exactly where it is; the clipboard is never overwritten with a command that forks a live session.
actual: 7/7 recorded jumps returned {ok:false, cmd:'cd <repo> && claude --resume <id>'} with one clipboard write each (vibepet 02:28:33 ×2 instances, 02:30:29; kestrel 02:47:06, 02:47:13, 02:50:10, 02:52:0x). tmux panes unchanged (session_attached=0, same window/pane). Bubble: 'couldn't find its terminal — resume command copied' although the pane exists; pasting the command would start a second claude on the live conversation.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S7/timings.json F2 'OS key → jump attempt finished' median 202 ms n=4
truth: vibepet idle/done in tmux pane vp-vibepet:0.0; kestrel question at end of turn (02:46:18.98) then permission prompt (02:50:26.0) in vp-kestrel:0.0; both live claude processes

why: 5/5 jumps from the jump key (kestrel ×4 incl. one from hidden, vibepet ×1) returned {ok:false, cmd:'cd …/fleet/<member> && claude --resume <live session id>'} in 74–92 ms (median 78, load 1.3–1.75), each with one (stubbed) clipboard write. tmux display for vp-kestrel:0.0 / vp-vibepet:0.0 read '0 1 1 @8 %8' / '0 1 1 @1 %1' before and after (no client attached, nothing selected). The registry names the pane ('tmux':'vp-kestrel:@8.%8') but the app never uses it; the copied command would start a second claude on a conversation that is live in its pane.
cause: main.js:696-715 (jump: no .app host -> clipboard.writeText(resume cmd) at main.js:714); agents.js:326-332 (hostApp only walks to an .app ancestor; the tmux server has none)
